newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann joins French Cegetel alliance.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann joins French Cegetel alliance.

text.p: German engineering and technology group Mannesmann AG said on Wednesday it had signed contracts to take a 15 percent stake in Cegetel, the rival phone alliance set to challenge monopoly France Telecom.
Other shareholders in the Cegetel group include British Telecom, which will hold 26 percent, Cie. Generale des Eaux, with 44 percent, and Southwestern Bell Telephone Co, with 15 percent.
Cegetel already had one million mobile phone customers in France and planned to offer a full range of telecommunications services when the french market deregulates completely in 1998.

Cegetel has access to an infrastructure covering all of france through Telecom Developpement (TD), a subsidiary of French railway SNCF. Mannesmann and Cie Generale des Eaux hold a joint participation in TD.
The partners have begun preparing to obtain regulatory approval for the deal.
SBC International is a unit of Southwestern Bell Corp. of the United States.
